title: The September-to-February high-water contrast rose by 9.2 cm at five Mid-Atlantic gauges between 1980-1999 and 2000-2020
abstract: We tested whether a larger seasonal mean sea-level contrast also occurs in monthly highest water at five Mid-Atlantic gauges. We used fixed NOAA records and paired September and February in each year. Between 1980-1999 and 2000-2020, the equal-gauge mean contrast rose by 10.36 cm for monthly mean level and 9.24 cm for monthly highest water. The change in highest water minus monthly mean was -1.12 cm, with a 95% three-year block interval from -7.78 to 5.67 cm. The data do not show a clear added seasonal change above the monthly mean. The gap result remains uncertain with other block lengths, common years, and an extension through 2025. The one-year interval for monthly highest change includes zero. The test does not identify storm change, flood frequency, or a physical cause. Missing observations, sampling changes, short periods, and slow ocean variation limit inference. Fixed paired evidence, exact raw-source hashes, code, bootstrap draws, and arithmetic checks support reproduction.

display.caption: September-minus-February contrasts and their changes between 1980-1999 and 2000-2020. Intervals use paired three-year blocks across all five gauges. Highest minus mean gives no clear added change.
